purpose: Every registry and owner file: who owns it, which code reads it, which test guards it. Agents read this first.
One name and one definition per business idea, in the client's words.
Same terms: status, source, the ask and the answer that settled it, where each term lives in data and code, proposed new terms.
User stories: what the owner wants, why, the human step, and when it counts as done.
Same ids: status, source, ask, decided, progress, blocking issue, where the runnable check is, data dependencies, notes, proposed rewording.
Business rules: when X, do Y; thresholds named, never numbered; the stories each rule serves.
Same ids: status, source, ask, decided, where the rule is implemented, notes, proposed rewording; a rule not yet approved is a proposed row here only.
Threshold defaults: the only place a number lives. A client's own value is a confirmed threshold fact, never an edit here.
Every business fact a client may state (costs, caps, limits): type, unit, bounds, required or not. Setting any other key is refused.
Per-entity decisions: value domain and whether a human must confirm (confirm = human) before it is in force.
The harness's own message codes: params and one meaning per language, checked both ways. The kit's codes live in the vendored kit, never here.
Alert rules as rows: grain, metric, comparison, threshold, cooldown. Read by the harness's own alert compute; the kit has no alert reader.
One read-only check per done story: a read verb, what its JSON must hold, which tables it needs.
Which build step (BUILD.md) the harness is at, who must sign each gate, and the answer, merge or pipeline that signed it.
